chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muammar ibn Khallaad, who said:

Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Al-Ma'mun said to me, "O Abu Al-Hasan, if you could write to some of those who obey you in these regions where our relationship has become strained." I said to him, "O Chief of the Believers, if you fulfill [your promise] to me, I will fulfill [my promise] to you. I have entered into this matter on the condition that I do not command, nor prohibit, nor appoint, nor dismiss, and this matter has not increased anything for me in terms of favor."'

"And I was in Medina, and my letter would reach the East and the West. I would ride my donkey and pass through the streets of Medina, and there was no one more prestigious than me in it, and no one among them would ask me for a need that I could fulfill, except that I would fulfill it for him."'
He said, 'I will fulfill [my promise] to you.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan, a title for Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ: The East and the West (referring to the breadth of the Caliphate)
key_terms.لَا آمُرَ وَلَا أَنْهَى: I do not command and do not prohibit (indicating lack of executive authority)

ai.seo_question: What were the conditions of Imam Al-Rida's acceptance of Al-Ma'mun's governorship?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the concept of *al-amr bi-l-ma'ruf wa al-nahy 'an al-munkar* in its passive form, where Imam Al-Rida (AS) accepted the political role of heir apparent under Caliph Al-Ma'mun but explicitly reserved the right to abstain from executive authority (commanding, prohibiting, appointing, or dismissing). The Imam contrasts this nominal status with his previous humble life in Medina, where his personal presence and direct interaction with the people carried more spiritual and social weight than formal power, highlighting the Shia preference for authentic religious influence over political prestige.

en.hubeali: H 14582 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muammar Bin Khallaad who said:

Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws said to me: ‘Al-Ma’moun said to measws, ‘O Abu Al-Hassanasws, if youasws could write to some of the ones who are obedient to youasws in these areas in which their relationship with us is spoilt’. Iasws said to him: ‘O Chief of believers, if you fulfil (your commitment) to measws, Iasws would (fulfil myasws commitment) to you, but rather, Iasws have entered into this matter in which Iasws have been entered into, Iasws do not issue commands, nor do Iasws prohibit, nor do Iasws appoint anyone, nor do Iasws dismiss anyone, and this matter which Iasws have entered into has not increased anything for measws regarding the favours.

And I<sup>asws</sup> used to be in Al-Medina, and my<sup>asws</sup> letter would be established in the east and the west, and I<sup>asws</sup> would ride upon my<sup>asws</sup> mule and pass by in the markets of Al-Medina, and there would be no one more prestigious than me<sup>asws</sup>, and there was none among them who would question me<sup>asws</sup> for a need with the possibility of my<sup>asws</sup> fulfilling it, except that I<sup>asws</sup> would fulfill it for him’.
He said, ‘I will fulfill (my commitment) to you<sup>asws</sup>’.
